items.description: Cancellation boundaries still require reciprocal concurrent-delivery links after the revised requirements explicitly tolerate one-sided declarations.
items.analysis: The revised acceptance criterion correctly permits an existing matching declaration in either direction, but the later requirement and boundary retain the former reciprocal-only wording. That leaves the durable contract internally inconsistent with the paired skill guidance.
items.recommendation: Replace the remaining reciprocal-only wording with the same explicit-declaration and matching-surviving-relationship rule.
items.rationale: Keep the requirements and boundaries consistent with the intentional tolerance of one-sided explicit declarations.

items.description: Cancellation mutation could be interrupted between updating related records and archiving the target.
items.analysis: The workflow spans Git-tracked lifecycle records, so an interrupted manual operation could leave an intermediate worktree state. The reported scenario is not a supported concurrent-operation case, and existing runtime validation exposes an invalid active cancelled record rather than silently accepting it.
items.recommendation: Add transactional mutation or a recovery procedure.
items.rationale: Do not introduce transaction or recovery machinery for a speculative interruption scenario; retain the focused validation and recoverable Git history.

items.description: Concurrent lifecycle operations could overwrite overlapping record updates.
items.analysis: Specle does not support simultaneous lifecycle operations against the same checkout and records. Separate worktrees produce ordinary Git divergence or conflict before shared state is silently overwritten.
items.recommendation: Serialize lifecycle mutations or reject stale whole-record writes.
items.rationale: This adds concurrency machinery for an unsupported hypothetical workflow rather than addressing an observed lifecycle defect.

items.description: Cancellation guidance does not state a separate response when required checkout inspection fails.
items.analysis: A failed Git inspection is possible only through an exceptional environment failure such as a damaged or inaccessible worktree. It is not cancellation-specific, and ordinary agent work already cannot proceed reliably without its required tools.
items.recommendation: Add an explicit stop-and-request-direction rule for failed Git inspection.
items.rationale: Workflow guidance assumes its required tools are working; do not add defensive cancellation-specific prose for exceptional tool failure.

items.description: A dependency added after cancellation discovery could survive in another active record.
items.analysis: The proposal assumes concurrent mutation by another actor during the cancellation window. The workflow already re-reads confirmed affected records immediately before writing, and concurrent lifecycle mutation is not a supported model.
items.recommendation: Rescan every active dependency array immediately before mutation and repeat confirmation for newly found dependents.
items.rationale: Do not add repeated discovery and confirmation loops for an unsupported concurrent-mutation scenario.

items.description: A one-sided concurrent-delivery declaration can survive when its named target is cancelled.
items.analysis: The current guidance discovers only relationships declared by the target. A malformed existing declaration in the other direction would not be removed before the target archive move.
items.recommendation: Stop cancellation and require relationship repair before archiving.
items.rationale: Tolerate a missing declaration in either direction. Discover relevant existing declarations on either record and, after confirmation, remove only the matching surviving entry; do not block cancellation merely because the reciprocal declaration is absent.

items.description: Cancelling a committed parent before its committed concurrent sidecar can strand the sidecar's parent-owned finalisation path.
items.analysis: The existing lifecycle permits a deliberate, safe order: handle the shared PR as directed, cancel each explicitly named committed sidecar first, then cancel the now-unlinked parent. Cancelling the parent first removes that ordered route.
items.recommendation: Require a separate finalisation plan before unlinking a committed partner.
items.rationale: When cancelling a committed parent with committed concurrent sidecars, stop before mutation and explain the correct course: handle the shared PR as directed, explicitly cancel each sidecar first, then retry cancellation of the parent. Do not create a new finalisation mechanism.

items.description: The cancellation timestamp test combines diagnostics from separate invalid fixtures.
items.analysis: The existing requirements incorrectly promote timestamp presence to a runtime validity condition. The schema already makes lifecycle timestamps optional, and normal workflows should write them without treating absent historical or partial metadata as invalid.
items.recommendation: Identify the archived fixture's missing-evidence diagnostic explicitly.
items.rationale: `cancelled_at` and `archived_at` are SHOULD metadata: normal cancellation and archival procedures write them, but their absence is not an error. Remove the cancellation timestamp validity requirement and its diagnostic test rather than tightening it.

items.description: Runtime lifecycle validation rejects a cancelled spike.
items.analysis: The cancel lifecycle declares generic transitions from defined and spiking to cancelled, but spike validation currently derives statuses only from explicitly spike-scoped transitions. A cancelled spike would therefore be invalid.
items.recommendation: Allow generic terminal cancellation for a spike without admitting unrelated planning or implementation statuses, and add a regression test.
items.rationale: Confirmed defect: cancellation explicitly accepts spikes, so a cancelled spike must validate.

items.description: Cancelling one member of a reciprocal concurrent-delivery pair leaves the surviving record invalid.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-2; independently confirmed in src/specle/lifecycle.py and the reciprocal relationship contract.
items.analysis: Concurrent-delivery relationships are explicit reciprocal records rather than dependencies. Archiving only one member leaves the other pointing to a missing active record and blocks validation and delivery.
items.recommendation: Detect only an explicit reciprocal concurrent-delivery partner, require confirmation, then remove only that reciprocal relationship from the surviving active record in the same recoverable mutation.
items.rationale: Preserve one-target cancellation while requiring an explicit, confirmed unlink of the known surviving partner; do not infer or cancel additional work.

items.description: Runtime validation permits cancelled records without their required archive location or timestamp.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-3; independently confirmed in src/specle/lifecycle.py and the cancellation requirements.
items.analysis: The shared schema keeps lifecycle timestamps optional, so runtime lifecycle validation must enforce cancellation-specific evidence and location. It currently permits active cancelled records and archived cancelled records without cancelled_at.
items.recommendation: Require cancelled_at for cancelled records, reject cancelled records outside the archive, derive terminal acceptance through the existing helper, and add focused negative tests.
items.rationale: The requirements explicitly define both invariants, and validating them keeps interrupted cancellation mutations visible.

items.description: Cancellation guidance ambiguously forbids selected targets and omits direct-delivery consequences.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-4; independently confirmed in the cancel and commit skill guidance.
items.analysis: The target must be explicit, not inferred from the selector, but an explicitly named selected target is valid. Direct/local delivery has recorded branch and commit evidence without a PR, which also requires user-directed handling.
items.recommendation: Clarify explicit-name selection, surface direct/local delivery evidence before cancellation, and stop the dependency scan before mutation when an active status record is unreadable or malformed.
items.rationale: These corrections preserve the intended user-directed handling of selected and already delivered work.

items.description: Adjacent lifecycle guidance still treats complete as the sole terminal archive outcome.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-5; independently confirmed in the lifecycle policy and activate and explain skills.
items.analysis: A worktree-local selector can remain after another worktree archives its target as cancelled. Guidance must treat that archived target as terminal and replaceable, while read-only explanation must cover both terminal outcomes.
items.recommendation: Synchronise blueprint and installed policy, activate, and explain guidance for cancelled selector cleanup, replacement, updated_at, and archival inspection.
items.rationale: This prevents a stale local selector from blocking future activation and completes the documented terminal-state model.

items.description: Regression tests omit broad cancellation workflow-guidance assertions.
items.analysis: The accepted runtime defects need focused executable coverage, but the proposed remaining tests would repeatedly test agent-executed Markdown workflow prose and simulate cancellation scenarios in the regular suite.
items.recommendation: Add broad packaged-skill and guidance-contract tests.
items.rationale: Keep the suite focused on executable runtime and schema invariants; agent-guidance scenarios are verified directly rather than through recurring workflow simulation.

items.description: The review record uses findings instead of the established items collection.
items.evidence: .specle/agy-add-change-cancel.json: AGY-7; independently confirmed in src/specle/lifecycle.py and docs/LAYOUT.md.
items.analysis: Resolved-review validation reads items. Retaining findings would make a later resolved review invalid despite an otherwise valid record.
items.recommendation: Use the established items collection while preserving all current source records and dispositions.
items.rationale: The review record must use the documented collection consumed by runtime validation.
